public_rationale: Contemporaneous coverage identifies the Cybercab as a prototype and places production in the future. The invitation-only demonstration did not establish that a production robotaxi or public service had arrived. Demonstration rides are consistent with this reading of Zitron's criticism.
limitations: This assesses availability at the event and publication, not subsequent deployment.
The conclusion relies on contemporaneous news coverage because the attempted primary event sources did not yield usable text.
The word arrived could also describe an unveiling; that is not the reading used here.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Tesla's robotaxi has not arrived; the We, Robot event showed only a prototype and a speech.

statement.excerpt: It isn’t. You saw a prototype and heard a speech.
statement.document_title: You Can't Make Friends With The Rockstars

our_interpretation: In context, arrived means a production robotaxi or publicly available robotaxi service, rather than an unveiled demonstration vehicle.
The target is the October 10–11 event and its status through the October 14 publication date.
Only a prototype and a speech describes the product's availability; it does not deny that demonstration rides occurred.
criteria.support_condition: The event presented prototype vehicles and future production plans, without launching the claimed production product or public robotaxi service.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The event launched a production robotaxi available to customers or an operating public robotaxi service.
